> **17131(SQLSTATE: 2F000) no choices may appear with choice OTHERS in an exception handler**

<a id="a788d386341a3975"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The OTHERS handler and another exception handler can not be used together in EXCEPTION WHEN clause.<br><br>gSQL&gt;<br>DECLARE<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;e1 EXCEPTION;<br>BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;RAISE e1;<br>EXCEPTION WHEN e1 OR OTHERS THEN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE( 'exception variable OR others' );<br>END;<br>/<br><br>ERR-2F000(17032): PSM compilation error :<br>(1) at (5:22): ERR-2F000(17131): no choices may appear with choice OTHERS in an exception handler</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Exclude the exception handler used with OTHERS handler, or configure it as a separate exception handler.<br><br>DECLARE<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;e1 EXCEPTION;<br>BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;RAISE e1;<br>EXCEPTION WHEN e1 THEN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE( 'exception variable' );<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;WHEN OTHERS THEN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE( 'OR others' );<br>END;<br>/<br><br>Anonymous PL block executed.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **17132 (SQLSTATE: OW000): cannot execute in a trigger (%s)**

<a id="403468b956098c63"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">DDL or DCL statements were specified in the trigger body.<br><br>gSQL&gt; CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER tri1<br>AFTER INSERT ON t1<br>BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'CREATE TABLE t2 ( c1 INTEGER , c2 INTEGER )';<br>END;<br>/<br>Trigger created.<br><br>gSQL&gt; INSERT INTO t1( c1, c2 ) VALUES( 1, 1 );<br>ERR-0W000(17132): cannot execute in a trigger (CREATE TABLE t2 ( c1 INTEGER , c2 INTEGER )) :<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'CREATE TABLE t2 ( c1 INTEGER , c2 INTEGER )';<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;*<br>ERROR at line 4:<br>ERROR at TRIGGER("TRI1")</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">DDL or DCL statements cannot be specified in the trigger body.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **17133 (SQLSTATE: OW000): cannot insert into a generated always identity column (%s.%s)**

<a id="7ebb9692903e3809"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">A column with the IDENTITY property is specified in the trigger body.<br><br>gSQL&gt; CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER tri3<br>BEFORE UPDATE ON t3<br>REFERENCING NEW ROW AS n_row<br>FOR EACH ROW<br>BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;n_row.c1 := 100;<br>END;<br>/<br>ERR-01000(16659): Warning: trigger "PUBLIC"."TRI1" has compilation errors :<br>(1) : ERR-0W000(17133): cannot insert into a generated always identity column (N_ROW.C1)<br>Trigger created.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Remove the IDENTITY property of that column to activate the trigger.<br><br>gSQL&gt; ALTER TABLE t3 ALTER COlUMN c1 DROP IDENTITY;<br>Table altered.<br><br>gSQL&gt; CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER tri3<br>BEFORE UPDATE ON t3<br>REFERENCING NEW ROW AS n_row<br>FOR EACH ROW<br>BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;n_row.c1 := 100;<br>END;<br>/<br>Trigger created.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **17134 (SQLSTATE: OW000): TRIGGER(%s) compilation error**

<a id="4900755d5be00ab2"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">deprecated</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **17135 (SQLSTATE: 2F002): modifying SQL-data not permitted**

<a id="e48d9808b6e6417f"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>This is a PL statement that violates the Routine’s SQL-Data Access Indicator.<br><br>gSQL&gt; CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE proc_callee MODIFIES SQL DATA AS<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE( 'success' );<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;END;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/<br>Procedure created.<br><br>gSQL&gt; CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE proc_caller READS SQL DATA AS<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;proc_callee;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;END;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/<br>ERR-01000(16409): Warning: Routine(PROC_CALLER) has compilation errors :<br>(1) at (3:3): ERR-2F002(17135): modifying SQL-data not permitted<br>Procedure created.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Write the PL statement so that it complies with the Routine’s SQL-Data Access Indicator.<br><br>gSQL&gt; CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE proc_caller MODIFIES SQL DATA AS<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;proc_callee;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;END;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/<br>Procedure created.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **17136 (SQLSTATE: 2F003): prohibited SQL-statement attempted**

<a id="25e9c2d61712a367"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **17137 (SQLSTATE: 2F004): reading SQL-data not permitted**

<a id="6564fd8421167125"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>This is a PL statement that violates the Routine’s SQL-Data Access Indicator.<br><br>gSQL&gt; CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION func_readssqldata RETURN INTEGER READS SQL DATA AS<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;RETURN 20;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;END;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/<br>Function created.<br><br>gSQL&gt; CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE proc1 CONTAINS SQL AS<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;var1 INTEGER;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;var1 := func_readssqldata;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;END;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/<br>ERR-01000(16409): Warning: Routine(PROC1) has compilation errors :<br>(1) at (4:11): ERR-2F004(17137): reading SQL-data not permitted<br>Procedure created.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Write the PL statement so that it complies with the Routine’s SQL-Data Access Indicator.<br><br>gSQL&gt; CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE proc1 READS SQL DATA AS<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;var1 INTEGER;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;var1 := func_readssqldata;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;END;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/<br>Procedure created.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **17138 (SQLSTATE: 2F000): package variables are available only within PSM**

<a id="f35d05211fd0a614"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>A package public variable was used directly in an SQL statement.<br><br>gSQL&gt;<br>CREATE OR REPLACE PACKAGE pkg5 AS<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;var1 INTEGER;<br>END;<br>/<br>Package created.<br><br>gSQL&gt;<br>DECLARE<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;v_sql_text varchar(100);<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;ref1 SYS_REFCURSOR;<br>BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;v_sql_text := 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t1 WHERE c1 = pkg5.var1';<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;OPEN ref1 FOR v_sql_text;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;CLOSE ref1;<br>END;<br>/<br><br>ERR-2F000(17138): package variables are available only within PSM :<br>SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t1 WHERE c1 = pkg5.var1<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;*<br>ERROR at line 1:</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>To use a package public variable in an SQL statement, the USING clause, INTO clause, or similar mechanisms must be used.<br><br>gSQL&gt;<br>DECLARE<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;v_sql_text varchar(100);<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;ref1 SYS_REFCURSOR;<br>BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;v_sql_text := 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t1 WHERE c1 = ?';<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;OPEN ref1 FOR v_sql_text using in pkg5.var1;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;CLOSE ref1;<br>END;<br>/<br><br>Anonymous PL block executed.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **17139 (SQLSTATE: 2F000): the type of table function parameter should be scalar**

<a id="d117915044a7ce56"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>ROWTYPE was used as the parameter type of a table function.<br><br>gSQL&gt;<br>CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION func1( p1 t1%ROWTYPE )<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;RETURN TABLE( c1 INTEGER, c2 INTEGER )<br>IS<br>BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;RETURN TABLE ( SELECT c1, c2 FROM t1 WHERE c1 = p1.c1 );<br>END;<br>/<br><br>ERR-2F000(17139): the type of table function parameter should be scalar :<br>CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION func1( p1 t1%ROWTYPE )<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;*<br>ERROR at line 1:</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Table function parameters must be of a scalar type.<br><br>gSQL&gt;<br>CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION func1( p1 INTEGER )<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;RETURN TABLE( c1 INTEGER, c2 INTEGER )<br>IS<br>BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;RETURN TABLE ( SELECT c1, c2 FROM t1 WHERE c1 = p1 );<br>END;<br>/<br><br>Function created.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **17140 (SQLSTATE: 2F000): RETURNING INTO clause can be used only in SQL statements that include RETURNING INTO**

<a id="1b3f3b551b0f6c0a"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The RETURNING INTO clause was used in an unsupported SQL statement.<br><br>gSQL&gt;<br>DECLARE<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;var1 INTEGER;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;var2 INTEGER;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;v_str VARCHAR(60);<br>BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;v_str := 'INSERT INTO t1 VALUES ( 2 , 2 ) RETURNING *';<br><br>&nbsp;&nbsp;EXECUTE IMMEDIATE v_str RETURNING INTO var1 , var2;<br>END;<br>/<br><br>ERR-2F000(17140): returning-into clause must be used with RETURNING INTO statements :<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;EXECUTE IMMEDIATE v_str RETURNING INTO var1 , var2;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;*<br>ERROR at line 8:</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>The RETURNING INTO clause can be used only in the following SQL statements.<br>&nbsp;• INSERT INTO name RETURNING .. INTO<br>&nbsp;• INSERT INTO name ... UPDATE RETURNING ... INTO<br>&nbsp;• DELETE FROM name RETURNING .. INTO<br>&nbsp;• UPDATE name RETURNING .. INTO<br><br>gSQL&gt;<br>DECLARE<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;var1 INTEGER;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;var2 INTEGER;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;v_str VARCHAR(60);<br>BEGIN<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;v_str := 'INSERT INTO t1 VALUES ( 2 , 2 ) RETURNING * INTO ? , ?';<br><br>&nbsp;&nbsp;EXECUTE IMMEDIATE v_str RETURNING INTO var1 , var2;<br>END;<br>/<br><br>Anonymous PL block executed.</td></tr></tbody></table>

<a id="8d6ed1373b2a8946"></a>
## Session Related Error

> **18000 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Invalid Statement**

<a id="74772cf63f6b6338"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>This error occurs when a client attempts to use a statement that has already been closed on the server side.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Create a new statement and execute the operation again.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18001 (SQLSTATE: HY024): Invalid attribute value**

<a id="bb984e880cdbc15f"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>This error occurs when setting a session property where the property identifier is valid, but an invalid value that is not applicable to the property is specified.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Set a valid value appropriate for the corresponding property.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18002 (SQLSTATE: HY092): Invalid attribute/option identifier**

<a id="e1b3b77caa0f688c"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>This error occurs when setting or retrieving a session property using a property identifier that does not exist or is not supported.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Use the correct property identifier.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18003 (SQLSTATE: 42000): Transaction is READ ONLY**

<a id="0f275636eccd1e90"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>This error occurs when executing the DML operation after changing the transaction attribute to read-only.<br><br>gSQL&gt; SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY;<br>Transaction set.<br><br>gSQL&gt; INSERT INTO t1 VALUES ( 1 );<br>ERR-42000(18003): Transaction is READ ONLY</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Execute the DML operation after changing the transaction attribute to read-write.<br><br>gSQL&gt; SET TRANSACTION READ WRITE;<br>Transaction set.<br><br>gSQL&gt; INSERT INTO t1 VALUES ( 1 );<br>1 row created.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18004 (SQLSTATE: 42000): Statement cannot execute as atomic action**

<a id="a7cbff8758e5e239"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">This error occurs when the statement cannot be executed because it is not an atomic insert.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Execute after turning the atomic option OFF in the driver.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18005 (SQLSTATE: 42000): Preparable phase is open phase**

<a id="ade992dece6d1f92"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">deprecated</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18006 (SQLSTATE: 08S01): Communication link failure**

<a id="23aa9d2b33a82851"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>This error occurs when a client attempts to use a session that has already been terminated on the server side.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Reconnect and try again.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18007 (SQLSTATE: HYC00): not implemented feature, in a function %s**

<a id="6fdacc2640e3142e"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18008 (SQLSTATE: HY014): Limit on the number of SQL statement exceeded**

<a id="7fb8833aefcfebd9"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The maximum number of statements that can be allocated in a single session has been exceeded.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Check whether the application is allocating statements using<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#c92b5d300715b0f4">SQLAllocStmt</a>&nbsp;without properly releasing them using<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#789c71d29f1ae76e">SQLFreeStmt</a>.<br>To increase the number of statements that can be used concurrently in a single session, modify the<a href="../part-02-administration-manual/10-server-property.md#5b8124ef92ae7188">MAXIMUM_CONCURRENT_ACTIVITIES</a>&nbsp;property.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18009 (SQLSTATE: 42000): The command cannot be executed when global transaction is in the ACTIVE state**

<a id="ce78cc0002480f4c"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">This error occurs when an attempt is made to execute a command that is not compatible with the transaction while the XA transaction has not yet been committed or rolled back.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Execute after the XA transaction is terminated.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18010 (SQLSTATE: 07009): Invalid descriptor index**

<a id="bbb7d5771b575a84"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">An invalid parameter index was specified when retrieving parameter information from the SQL statement.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Check the number of parameters in the SQL statement and use a parameter index within the valid range.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18011 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Character set not equal(%s and %s)**

<a id="68d5ad10a6e1b688"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18012 (SQLSTATE: HY010): fetch out of sequence**

<a id="bcd399215e15543b"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">An attempt was made to fetch data from a cursor that was already closed due to a transaction commit, rollback, or savepoint rollback.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Check whether the cursor is still valid. If necessary, reopen the cursor or use the with-hold option to keep the cursor open after the transaction ends.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18013 (SQLSTATE: HYC00): Optional feature not implemented**

<a id="2689fae16af953bb"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">Isolation levels such as READ UNCOMMITTED are defined in the SQL standard but are considered auxiliary options that are not actually supported.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Use options such as READ COMMITTED or SERIALIZABLE.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18014 (SQLSTATE: 07001): Wrong number of parameters**

<a id="67707f7b64974dea"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The number of parameters required by the SQL statement does not match the number of parameters actually bound.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Verify the number of parameters required by the SQL statement.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18015 (SQLSTATE: 24000): Invalid cursor state**

<a id="6792f0ddfd952943"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">An attempt was made to change the cursor position while the cursor was not open or the result set was not prepared.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">First, execute the SQL statement to generate the result set and open the cursor. Then, ensure the cursor is in a valid state before performing any positioning operations.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18016 (SQLSTATE: 42000): remote xa transaction (%d.%ld) already exists**

<a id="e3d752362133959e"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">This error occurs when an attempt is made to start a new XA transaction while an active XA transaction already exists.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Execute after the XA transaction is terminated.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **18017 (SQLSTATE: 42000): remote xa transaction (%d.%ld) does not exist**

<a id="23cc4c9d260863c8"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">This error occurs when the XA transaction corresponding to the specified transaction ID cannot be found.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Check whether the XA transaction has been terminated or if the transaction ID is correct.</td></tr></tbody></table>

<a id="80239e306b59435b"></a>
## ODBC Related Error

> **19000 (SQLSTATE: HY009): Invalid use of null pointer**

<a id="1d681083497e3443"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The argument is NULL and it is not valid.<br>An error occurred in the following example because the third parameter was output argument but NULL was used.<br><br>SQLAllocHandle( SQL_HANDLE_STMT, dbc, NULL );</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check ODBC API, and use the variable which is valid for the argument.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19001 (SQLSTATE: HY092): Invalid attribute/option identifier**

<a id="8e0626719262d4f8"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The property which is not supported by each HANDLE type was used, or the property value was missing when setting the property.<br><br>For example, the first argument of SQLAllocHandle function is the handle type to be allocated, so an error occurs if the data other than SQL_HANDLE_ENV, SQL_HANDLE_DBC, SQL_HANDLE_STMT, SQL_HANDLE_DESC is used.<br><br>SQLAllocHandle( -1, dbc, &amp;stmt );</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check ODBC API, and check available properties and options.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19002 (SQLSTATE: 08003): Connection not open**

<a id="8bc557db21aa6f54"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>SQLHDBC handle is not OPEN.<br>If allocating SQLHSTMT handle right after allocating SQLHDBC handle without connecting as follows, then an error occurs.<br><br>SQLAllocHandle( SQL_HANDLE_DBC, env, &amp;dbc );<br>SQLAllocHandle( SQL_HANDLE_STMT, dbc, &amp;stmt );</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>If the connecting is required, then connect to DB first through SQLConnect or SQLDriverConnect function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19003 (SQLSTATE: IM001): Driver does not support this function**

<a id="68ba08eed4f3cb47"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The function or feature which is currently not supported was used.<br>It does not support allocating SQLHDESC handle with SQLAllocHandle function as follows.<br><br>SQLAllocHandle( SQL_HANDLE_DESC, dbc, &amp;desc );</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check the supported function or feature.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19004 (SQLSTATE: IM004): Driver's SQLAllocHandle on SQL_HANDLE_ENV failed**

<a id="ba7b8427724e2990"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19005 (SQLSTATE: IM005): Driver's SQLAllocHandle on SQL_HANDLE_DBC failed**

<a id="9e2aceef475407c9"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19006 (SQLSTATE: 08002): Connection name in use**

<a id="dec52e7de43327a3"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>SQLHDBC handle is already connected to the server.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>SQLHDBC handle connected to the server can not be connected again.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19007 (SQLSTATE: HY090): Invalid string or buffer length**

<a id="52d3e698a75bc410"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The string data length or the buffer length is not valid.<br><br>The following code inquires the data through SQLGetData function. If the variable bufLen value is smaller than 0, then this error occurs.<br>SQLGetData( stmt, 1, SQL_C_CHAR, buf, bufLen, &amp;ind );<br><br>The following code connects to the server through SQLConnect function. If the variable userName, auth length is smaller than or equal to 0, then this error occurs.<br>SQLConnect( dbc, serverName, serverNameLen, userName, userNameLen, auth, authLen, );</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check API of each function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19008 (SQLSTATE: 28000): Invalid authorization specification**

<a id="42631de6dbcf7b64"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">It is connected by using SQLDriverConnect function, but the user name or password length is 0.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Input a valid user name and a password.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19009 (SQLSTATE: HY010): Function sequence error**

<a id="4664244b5b0dbae3"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The current status of HANDLE is not valid.<br>The following code allocates SQLHDBC handle right after allocating SQLHENV handle.<br>SQLAllocEnv( &amp;env );<br>SQLAllocConnect( env, &amp;dbc );<br><br>An error occurs because SQL_ATTR_ODBC_VERSION property of SQLHENV handle was not set before allocating SQLHDBC handle.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the status transition table of HANDLE in MSDN ODBC document.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19010 (SQLSTATE: 24000): Invalid cursor state**

<a id="fd95c4d573bde970"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The transition status of SQLHSTMT handle is not valid.<br>For example, if SQLHSTMT handle is not prepared, or SQLCloseCursor function is called in execution without the result set, then this error occurs.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check the handle status available for each function. Check the status transition table in MSDSN ODBC document.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19011 (SQLSTATE: HY012): Invalid transaction operation code**

<a id="b0a247c91528ce37"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The value other than SQL_COMMIT, SQL_ROLLBACK was used as an argument of the transaction processing function SQLEndTran or SQLTransact.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#cb149adc5b93928b">SQLEndTran</a>, and use the correct value.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19012 (SQLSTATE: HYC00): Optional feature not implemented**

<a id="9b23bf1d0e3fd10e"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>Goldilocks driver used unsupported option or the option which was not compatible with the current SQLHDBC handle property. For example, SQLHDBC handle using the global connection causes an error when setting XA property.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#dd8da204f184f562">ODBC API References</a>.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19013 (SQLSTATE: HY003): Invalid application buffer type**

<a id="950c5bf5095b8853"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The invalid C data type identifier was used.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Refer to the data type defined in<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#7a948096d031d2a9">C data type</a>&nbsp;and ODBC standards.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19014 (SQLSTATE: 07009): Invalid descriptor index**

<a id="6166d500cb5d5a20"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The invalid index was used.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Modify the index number.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19015 (SQLSTATE: HY004): Invalid SQL data type**

<a id="81b00b1de3e62e52"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The invalid SQL type identifier was used.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Refer to the data type defined in<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#931aee0de9f03c02">SQL data type</a>&nbsp;and ODBC standards.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19016 (SQLSTATE: HY105): Invalid parameter type**

<a id="afaf4c3bfdc1a7da"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The parameter type is not valid.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#807cdb95ca6430e9">InputOutputType argument</a>.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19017 (SQLSTATE: HY009): Invalid argument value**

<a id="feee6de40843d9e9"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The variable used as an argument of the parameter storing the data is NULL, or the buffer length is 0.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>The variable storing the data when inquiring the data should have the valid length.<br>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#240d469b129b2980">SQLGetData</a>.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19018 (SQLSTATE: HY011): Attribute cannot be set now**

<a id="6fbaf3c151ce05f5"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The property can not be set in the transition status of the current handle.<br>For example, it tried to set SQL_ATTR_CHARACTER_SET, SQL_ATTR_LOCALITY_AWARE_TRANSACTION or SQL_ATTR_USE_GLOBAL_SESSION after SQLHDBC&nbsp;&nbsp;handle was connected.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check the property which can be set in the transition status of each handle.<br>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#a2ddb5cc3c0b2f7e">SQLSetConnectAttr</a>&nbsp;and<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#36bfe523796f6177">SQLSetStmtAttr</a>.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19019 (SQLSTATE: HY024): Invalid attribute value**

<a id="abea0eb081a3c645"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The handle property to be set is not a valid identifier.<br>The variable used as the property value related to each handle has the invalid value.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check the handle property to be set.<br>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#a2ddb5cc3c0b2f7e">SQLSetConnectAttr</a>&nbsp;and<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#36bfe523796f6177">SQLSetStmtAttr</a>.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19020 (SQLSTATE: 25000): Invalid transaction state**

<a id="2607bb595d7a7261"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>SQLHDBC handle called SQLDisconnect function while the transaction exists.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Call SQLDisconnect function after COMMIT or ROLLBACK the transaction related to SQLHDBC handle.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19021 (SQLSTATE: HY000): General error**

<a id="01c496214b9ac393"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>If the error related to SQLHSTMT handle occurs while getting the information about the driver in SQLGetInfo function, then the error message is added to the error.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>&nbsp;Check the error message through<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#352b96fc0e4bc1bf">SQLGetDiagRec</a>&nbsp;function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19022 (SQLSTATE: 07005): Prepared statement not a cursor-specification**

<a id="e41a9d4bec67a5fc"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The column was inquired for SQLHSTMT handle which is a prepared statement without the result set.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Call<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#53951ce9e5f367b0">SQLDescribeCol</a>,<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#45b1f743e1a4507f">SQLColAttribute</a>&nbsp;and<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#cd5a3951174466cb">SQLColAttributes</a>&nbsp;functions with SQLHSTMT&nbsp;&nbsp;handle having the result set.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19023 (SQLSTATE: 22001): String data, right truncated**

<a id="7fa0a1e33d815956"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>C data size is bigger than the column buffer size when converting C data to SQL data.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check the column length.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19024 (SQLSTATE: HY007): Associated statement is not prepared**

<a id="352156c03fcf944d"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>SQLHDESC handle tried to get the description information, but the transition status of SQLHSTMT handle was not valid.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#25a5e092f9cd04a3">SQLGetDescField</a>&nbsp;and<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#3945ff5d8c1b1eed">SQLGetDescRec</a>&nbsp;functions.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19025 (SQLSTATE: HY092): Option type out of range**

<a id="701a856dc2ebb1ce"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The option is not valid.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check the option available in SQLFreeStmt function.<br>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#789c71d29f1ae76e">SQLFreeStmt</a>.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19026 (SQLSTATE: 22002): Indicator variable required but not supplied**

<a id="684683494498e058"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>If the indicator is NULL when the data is NULL while inquiring the data, then an error occurs.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Use the indicator argument.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19027 (SQLSTATE: 01S01): Error in row**

<a id="02446c762a96c843"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19028 (SQLSTATE: HY016): Cannot modify an implementation row descriptor**

<a id="ac1b7b566830c43b"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The property of IRD descriptor handle can not be modified.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#1b41252aaf5c5156">SQLSetDescField</a>&nbsp;and<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#222903e597037a4f">SQLSetDescRec</a>&nbsp;functions.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19029 (SQLSTATE: HY091): Invalid descriptor field identifier**

<a id="6ba0150aa7d87294"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The property of SQLHDESC handle is not valid.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#1b41252aaf5c5156">SQLSetDescField</a>&nbsp;function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19030 (SQLSTATE: 07006): Restricted parameter value violation**

<a id="65ea7e5220e04bb7"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The type can not be converted when converting data type from C type to SQL type or from SQL type to C type.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check the type transition of MSDN ODBC.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19031 (SQLSTATE: 22015): Interval field overflow**

<a id="e25341cbdb9c52f5"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>An error occurred during the type transition of the interval type.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the type compatible with the interval type.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19032 (SQLSTATE: 22003): Numeric value out of range**

<a id="5273cd9272761f0e"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The size of the buffer to store the numeric data is smaller than the data length.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the error message and increase the buffer size.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19033 (SQLSTATE: 01004): String data, right truncated**

<a id="e3c881dfd97fada1"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The buffer length is smaller than the data length when inquiring the data.<br>The buffer length is insufficient when getting the handle property value.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check the error message and increase the buffer size.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19034 (SQLSTATE: 22018): Invalid character value for cast specification**

<a id="05ea5ed99db3e080"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The conversion from C string type data to the numeric type is not valid.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check if C string data is a valid numeric data.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19035 (SQLSTATE: 01S07): Fractional truncation**

<a id="f74060e689dbfc62"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>C buffer length is insufficient while converting the column data to C data.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Increase the buffer length.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19036 (SQLSTATE: 22008): Datetime field overflow**

<a id="c58a74e62d8a6adf"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19037 (SQLSTATE: 22007): Invalid datetime format**

<a id="ff5a282122ecb975"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The date type C data is not valid.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the data. The date type data should follow the gregorian calendar.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19038 (SQLSTATE: 08S01): Communication link failure**

<a id="605938b0bd8847f1"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It was disconnected during the communication protocol.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the network environment.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19039 (SQLSTATE: HY000): An invalid SQL type has occurred**

<a id="c3435ef6c2d61745"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The data column type received in the server while inquiring the data in SQL_C_DEFAULT type is not valid.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19040 (SQLSTATE: 34000): Invalid cursor name**

<a id="e51eeda30223376d"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The cursor name is not valid.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>The maximum length the cursor name should be smaller than 128 bytes.<br>The cursor name can not start with SQL_CUR, SQLCUR.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19041 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Failed to atomic execution**

<a id="e417d4f97c7d0bf5"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>An error occurred while executing the batch after SQL_ATTR_ATOMIC_EXECUTION property value was set to SQL_ATOMIC_EXECUTION_ON.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check the error through<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#352b96fc0e4bc1bf">SQLGetDiagRec</a>&nbsp;and<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#8652e391007cc4f3">SQLGetDiagField</a>&nbsp;functions.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19042 (SQLSTATE: HY110): Invalid driver completion**

<a id="f83c82c07a754467"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The argument value of the driver completion used in SQLDriverConnect function is not valid.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#e172f2fa8687781b">SQLDriverConnect</a>&nbsp;function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19043 (SQLSTATE: IM012): DRIVER keyword syntax error**

<a id="4606cfcd04851e8b"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The connecting string is not valid.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>The syntax of the connecting string consists of the keyword and the value, and the property can be added with ';'.<br>The following is an example of the connecting string used in SQLDriverConnect.<br>"DSN=GOLDILOCKS;UID=TEST;PWD=test"</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19044 (SQLSTATE: 08001): Client unable to establish connection**

<a id="af2a94bbe0efdd5d"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The socket can not be initialized or IP address can not be acquired from the host name.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check if the host name and IP address are correctly set when getting IP address with the host name.<br>If an error occurs while initializing the socket, check the system error and respond to it.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19045 (SQLSTATE: HY096): Information type out of range**

<a id="7d2e3b2de0e3ba87"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The information type identifier which is obtained from SQLGetInfo function is not valid.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#c2dcfe03f0659b13">SQLGetInfo</a>&nbsp;function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19046 (SQLSTATE: IM002): Data source not found and no default driver specified**

<a id="0e3521b9751b02a0"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The given data source name was not found from odbc.ini file.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the data source name and odbc.ini file.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19047 (SQLSTATE: HY106): Fetch type out of range**

<a id="70087b7d86e9def6"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The fetch orientation identifier is not valid in SQLExtendedFetch or SQLFetchScroll functions.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#b80988b770c5a88b">SQLFetchScroll</a>&nbsp;function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19048 (SQLSTATE: HY100): Uniqueness option type out of range**

<a id="19d38bc5a2c92467"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The unique identifier in SQLStatistics function is not valid.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#a42e1bfe518c9b4c">SQLStatistics</a>&nbsp;function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19049 (SQLSTATE: HY101): Accuracy option type out of range**

<a id="debf030b73b236a1"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The reserved identifier in SQLStatistics function is not valid.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#a42e1bfe518c9b4c">SQLStatistics</a>&nbsp;function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19050 (SQLSTATE: HY097): Column type out of range**

<a id="19b8b93f248ee665"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The identifier type identifier in SQLSpecialColumns function is not valid.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#3c60153be4224bf6">SQLSpecialColumns</a>&nbsp;function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19051 (SQLSTATE: HY098): Scope type out of range**

<a id="594ea32f7c2db0cf"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The scope identifier in SQLSpecialColumns function is not valid.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#3c60153be4224bf6">SQLSpecialColumns</a>&nbsp;function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19052 (SQLSTATE: HY099): Nullable type out of range**

<a id="d640c9224e863bda"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The nullable identifier is not valid in SQLSpecialColumns function.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#3c60153be4224bf6">SQLSpecialColumns</a>&nbsp;function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19053 (SQLSTATE: HY021): Inconsistent descriptor information**

<a id="9654271db7cc019a"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The information about the descriptor handle is not valid.<br><br>The following code sets the SQL type of the parameter to SQL_INTERVAL_MONTH in SQLHSTMT handle, and changes SQL_DESC_DATETIME_INTERVAL_PRECISION property of IPD handle to 1, then sets the buffer pointer with SQL_DESC_DATA_PTR property.<br><br>ret = SQLBindParameter( stmt, 1, SQL_PARAM_INPUT, SQL_C_NUMERIC, SQL_INTERVAL_MONTH, 1, 0, numeric, sizeof( SQL_NUMERIC_STRUCT ), 0 );<br>ret = SQLGetStmtAttr( stmt, SQL_ATTR_IMP_PARAM_DESC, &amp;ipd, 0, NULL );<br>ret = SQLSetDescField( ipd, 1, SQL_DESC_DATETIME_INTERVAL_PRECISION, (SQLPOINTER) 1, 0 );<br>ret = SQLSetDescField( ipd, 1, SQL_DESC_DATA_PTR, dataPtr, 0 );<br><br>SQL_DESC_DATETIME_INTERVAL_PRECISION property is set to 1, but it exceeds the precision range of INTERVAL MONTH type (2~6). Therefore, an error occurs while setting SQL_DESC_DATA_PTR property.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#1b41252aaf5c5156">SQLSetDescField</a>&nbsp;function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19054 (SQLSTATE: 01S02): Option value changed**

<a id="2efc90d4c573af7c"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The cursor property of SQLHSTMT handle has been changed.<br>The following is a sample code in which the property is changed while using SELECT FOR UPDATE statement though the cursor property of SQLHSTMT handle was set to SQL_CONCUR_READ_ONLY, SQL_SENSITIVE. SQLExecDirect function returns SQL_SUCCESS_WITH_INFO.<br><br>ret = SQLSetStmtAttr( stmt, SQL_ATTR_CONCURRENCY, (SQLPOINTER)SQL_CONCUR_READ_ONLY, 0 );<br>ret = SQLSetStmtAttr( stmt, SQL_ATTR_CURSOR_SENSITIVITY, (SQLPOINTER)SQL_SENSITIVE, 0 );<br>ret = SQLExecDirect( stmt, (SQLCHAR*)"SELECT C1 FROM SAMPLE_TABLE FOR UPDATE", SQL_NTS );</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#04841cd200e28204">SQLExecDirect</a>,<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#0b76dab8dddaa8c1">SQLExecute</a>,<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#36bfe523796f6177">SQLSetStmtAttr</a>,<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#683d49eae3436a63">SQLPrepare</a>&nbsp;functions.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19055 (SQLSTATE: HY109): Invalid cursor position**

<a id="bc0ef569a9e45710"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>SQLSetPos function was called with SQLHSTMT handle having FOWARD_ONLY property. Or, the row number argument of SQLSetPos function is smaller than or equal to 0.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#d672fac0c5c3a337">SQLSetPos</a>&nbsp;function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19056 (SQLSTATE: HY107): Row value out of range**

<a id="1cf0bdcfe8d5782b"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The row number argument value of SQLSetPos function is bigger than the array size.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#d672fac0c5c3a337">SQLSetPos</a>&nbsp;function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19057 (SQLSTATE: HYT00): Timeout expired**

<a id="dd4cb939bf25c6ba"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It tried to connect to the server, but timeout occurred.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the network environment. Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#175141b22aca5789">SQLConnect</a>&nbsp;function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19058 (SQLSTATE: 2C000): Invalid or unknown NLS parameter value specified**

<a id="b2bbd76faa640ffa"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19059 (SQLSTATE: HY020): Attempt to concatenate a null value**

<a id="5e5fa0e4326c8173"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>SQL_NULL_DATA identifier was used in StrLen_or_ind argument when returning SQL_NEED_DATA and calling SQLPutData.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#6be563a78cf501f3">SQLPutData</a>&nbsp;function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19060 (SQLSTATE: HY019): Non-character and non-binary data sent in pieces**

<a id="512b1c16381b0cb6"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>SQL_NEED_DATA was returned from the type other than SQL_C_CHAR, SQL_C_WCHAR, SQL_C_BINARY types, and SQLPutData was called more than once.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#6be563a78cf501f3">SQLPutData</a>&nbsp;function.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19061 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Invalid 'odbc.ini' specification. property : [%s]**

<a id="9b2edea6a5733e7e"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The value set in the property of odbc.ini file is not valid.<br>For example, valid values allowed in CS_MODE property of odbc.ini file are default, shared and dedicated, and if another value is used then an error occurs.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/34-odbc.md#c0bc1af6b9e0ca88">Data Source Configuration</a>.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19062 (SQLSTATE: IM008): Dialog failed**

<a id="f2031142f2025122"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19063 (SQLSTATE: 40001): Transaction rollback**

<a id="9482e331cb763ce4"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19064 (SQLSTATE: 40003): Statement completion unknown**

<a id="8424c3c9ad3672c2"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19065 (SQLSTATE: 08S01): Communication link failure**

<a id="cba663749e337a9c"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>It was disconnected during the operation, so it was connected to ALTERNATE_SERVERS with FAILOVER, but the operation of SQLHSTMT handle failed, so SESSION FAILOVER failed.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Connect SQLHDBC handle again.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19066 (SQLSTATE: 01000): General warning**

<a id="4e529b203fb8430e"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>It was disconnected while executing SQLEndTran function with SQL_ROLLBACK, but failover succeeded.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>It is a warning, so no other action is required.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19067 (SQLSTATE: HY104): Invalid precision or scale value**

<a id="90f8039f40464126"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The value of the column size, the decimal digits, the precision or the scale of SQL type set as SQLBindParameter function is out of the valid range of the SQL type.<br>For example, the column size of SQL_CHAR type is minimum 1, maximum 2000. The column size of SQL_NUMERIC type is minimum 1, maximum 38, and the decimal digits is minimum -84, maximum 127.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check the valid size per each SQL type of the parameter.<br>Refer to<a href="../part-03-sql-manual/16-built-in-data-type-references.md#513777896d946002">Built-in Data Type References</a>.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19068 (SQLSTATE: 40003): Retry the transactional operations**

<a id="9ee87fa6367d48e0"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>Failover was executed during the operation, and it succeeded</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Execute the operation again.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19069 (SQLSTATE: 08S01): Failed to communicate with locator**

<a id="88ca97cfdcf45a91"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>It failed in the process of setting the connection properties LOCATOR_SERVICE and LOCATOR_DSN and getting the connection information from glocator.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the trace log and the connection information of glocator.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19070 (SQLSTATE: 08006): Unable to get cluster system information**

<a id="a2441ff4cd1ae5c2"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It can not get cluster system info when using the global connection.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19071 (SQLSTATE: HY000): startup cannot be performed on ipc**

<a id="28a8a8f5aba79610"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It tried to execute STARTUP when PROTOCOL_TYPE connects to the server in IPC.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19072 (SQLSTATE: IM006): Driver's SQLSetConnectAttr failed**

<a id="760734ce820ae166"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The database connection was successful, but an error occurred while applying the predefined connection attributes.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">This error is treated as a warning, and the connection attribute settings should be retried.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19073 (SQLSTATE: HY017): Invalid use of an automatically allocated descriptor handle**

<a id="1dd4aae00003b6d1"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">An attempt was made to directly set the implementation row descriptor (SQL_ATTR_IMP_ROW_DESC) or the implementation parameter descriptor (SQL_ATTR_IMP_PARAM_DESC).</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Remove any code that attempts to directly set the SQL_ATTR_IMP_ROW_DESC or SQL_ATTR_IMP_PARAM_DESC attributes.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **19074 (SQLSTATE: HY108): Concurrency option out of range**

<a id="174f7fa1fc0e6a28"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">An invalid cursor concurrency option was used.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Use one of the following values: SQL_CONCUR_READ_ONLY, SQL_CONCUR_LOCK, SQL_CONCUR_ROWVER, or SQL_CONCUR_VALUES.</td></tr></tbody></table>

<a id="6cf842c63e87160f"></a>
## JDBC Related Error

> **21000 (SQLSTATE: HV000): Not used error**

<a id="bf5db02f5a30181a"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21001 (SQLSTATE: 46001): Invalid connection url[%s]: [%s]**

<a id="bc6858a93fc8feda"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The given URL is invalid.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Check URL string in the following manual.<br><ul><li><a href="../part-05-developer-manual/35-jdbc.md#bab51f8282d0687d">Connection</a></li></ul></td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21002 (SQLSTATE: 46110): Unsupported feature: [%s]**

<a id="acc5ab81dbf33621"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The unsupported API is used.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>It is the unsupported API, so find a workaround.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21003 (SQLSTATE: 08S01): Invalid protocol: [%s]**

<a id="a0e20d5f26fa9f59"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The communication protocol is not valid. The response protocol should be received for the protocol sent to the server in the client program, but the sequence has an error.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department. The protocol sending/ receiving logging can be found by using the connection property protocol_log.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21004 (SQLSTATE: HV000): Invalid method call for read-only ResultSet**

<a id="d01e9db2e98a1757"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">There was an attempt to change the row location or manipulate the data in read only ResultSet.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Row location change and data manipulation is not possible in read only ResultSet.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21005 (SQLSTATE: 08003): The Connection is already closed**

<a id="7edbcd4ce55abd9b"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The connection object was already closed when it called the method. Or, it was disconnected during the communication protocol.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Check the method which can be called when the connection object is closed.<br>If the connection object is implicitly closed, then check the error message occurred during the disconnection.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21006 (SQLSTATE: 08003): The Statement is already closed**

<a id="a95a58e7fd4de74a"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The statement object was already closed when it called the method. Or, it was disconnected during the communication protocol.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Check the method which can be called when the statement object is closed.<br>If the statement object is implicitly closed, then the connection object may be closed.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21007 (SQLSTATE: 08003): The ResultSet is already closed**

<a id="cfae0d9cac459cf4"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The ResultSet object was already closed when it called the method. Or, an error for FETCH occurred or it was disconnected due to an error from the server when executing FETCH protocol.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Check the method which can be called when the ResultSet object is closed.<br>Check the error message occurred during FETCH protocol.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21008 (SQLSTATE: HV000): Invalid method call for forward-only ResultSet**

<a id="988da10f97998cbd"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It tried to change the location of forward only ResultSet.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Change the ResultSet type to scrollable.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21009 (SQLSTATE: HV000): Invalid Wrapper type: [%s]**

<a id="cf9011d65f7ee859"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The object used as an input argument is not the wrapper class of the class.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the object used as an input argument.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21010 (SQLSTATE: HV000): Invalid argument: [%s]**

<a id="c38ae0e2815f09f6"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The valid object of the argument used in the method is null or the value is wrong.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the manual of the method.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21011 (SQLSTATE: 08000): Cannot connect to the server: %s**

<a id="77ef01aaf3fb0886"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It tried to connect the socket to the given address, but it failed.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check if the host and port is not valid, or if the network is not available.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21012 (SQLSTATE: 08S01): Communication link failure: %s**

<a id="24ecdbc25eb695fd"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">It was disconnected during the communication.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Check the detailed error message. Check the error situation by using trace_log and protocol_log as connection properties.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21013 (SQLSTATE: HV000): A mandatory property is omitted: [%s]**

<a id="1573d27d13af75e0"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>A mandatory connection property is omitted among the connection properties.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>The mandatory connection properties are USER and PASSWORD.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21014 (SQLSTATE: HV000): Not a select query for executeQuery method**

<a id="04287a1b2c708514"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21015 (SQLSTATE: HV000): The statement has produced a ResultSet**

<a id="988a87e89d8f88d8"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>PreparedStatement object was created with SELECT statement in which ResultSet was created, and executeBatch or executeUpdate method was called.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Use execute or executeQuery method in the statement in which ResultSet is created.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21016 (SQLSTATE: HV000): This method cannot be called for a PreparedStatement**

<a id="c6deb9fbd7e9e7a4"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>execute, executeBatch, executeUpdate, executeQuery methods which use SQL string as arguments can not be used in PreparedStatement class.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Use Statement class instead of PreparedStatement class when using SQL string as an argument in those methods.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21017 (SQLSTATE: HV000): Parameter type[%s] is mismatch with previous type[%s] during batch**

<a id="f921bfd9f6f10b2f"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The data type set as the set message is different from the previously set data type during the batch execution.<br>The following is an example of setting the data to the string type after setting it as the integer type data.<br>PreparedStatement pstmt = con.prepareStatement( "INSERT INTO TEST VALUES (?) ");<br>pstmt.setObject(1, 10);<br>pstmt.addBatch();<br>pstmt.setObject(1, "20");<br><br>An error occurs because the string data "20" is different from the previously set data type.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>If data types are not same for the same parameter, then do not use the batch execution.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21018 (SQLSTATE: HV000): Lack of parameter: [%s]'th parameter**

<a id="e0555631acde6966"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The parameter in which the data is not set exists.<br>The following code has two parameters, but the data is not set in the second parameter. An error occurs when calling execute method.<br>PreparedStatement pstmt = con.prepareStatement( "INSERT INTO TEST VALUES( ?, ? )" );<br>pstmt.setObject(1, 10);<br>pstmt.execute();</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Set the data in the parameter in which the data is missing.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21019 (SQLSTATE: HV000): No batch job added**

<a id="f1c63d975118f47c"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">deprecated</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21020 (SQLSTATE: HV000): Batch job added**

<a id="fdb10f33839c8436"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">execute, executeQuery or executeUpdate other than executeBatch method was called after calling addBatch method.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Call executeBatch method after calling addBatch method to use the batch execution.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21021 (SQLSTATE: 22003): The value[%s] is out of range of [%s] type**

<a id="943b2e24f934b4ee"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>It exceeds the range of the data type when setting the data in PreparedStatement class.<br>The following is the code exceeding the range of the data type while setting the string type data as the integer type.<br>PreparedStatement pstmt = con.prepareStatement("INSERT INTO TEST VALUES(?)");<br>pstmt.setObject( 1, "1000000000000", Types.INTEGER );<br><br>It exceeds the range of the data type when getting the data from ResultSet class.<br>The following is the code getting the numeric data 100 as a boolean type. An error occurs that it exceeds the range when calling getBoolean method from ResultSet.<br>pstmt.setInt( 1, 100 );<br>pstmt.execute();<br>ResultSet rs = stmt.executeQuery( "SELECT C1 FROM TEST" );<br>boolean isTrue = rs.getBoolean(1);</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Use the data type according to the table schema. If the table schema is unknown, then use getObejct, setObject methods.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21022 (SQLSTATE: 22026): The value length is mismatch[%s != %s]**

<a id="f63f64157f1fc3b4"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The data was set in ROWID type, but the data size violates ROWID type.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the data size in the error message.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21023 (SQLSTATE: HV000): The value([%s] type) cannot be converted to [%s] type**

<a id="46e6fede1ba0746d"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It tried to convert the data to the nonconvertible type.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/35-jdbc.md#1f1a9557cf30f535">Type Conversion</a>.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21024 (SQLSTATE: 08000): The connection timeout expired: [%s millis]**

<a id="a715a9491f3544eb"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It may occur because the server does not respond while connecting.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the network environment or check the connection property login_timeout.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21025 (SQLSTATE: HV000): The column is not found: [%s]**

<a id="426a97b0fd7479e3"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">It tried to retrieve or set the data with the column name in ResuletSet or PreparedStatement class, but the column name does not exist.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Check the column name.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21026 (SQLSTATE: 3B000): Savepoint error: %s**

<a id="cb4a24fee27644da"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The savepoint has ID or a name. This error occurs when retrieving ID of the savepoint using the name or retrieving the savepoint name using ID.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">The savepoint has ID or a name, and it should be retrieved according to the created savepoint.<br>The following is the code creating and retrieving the savepoint.<br>Savepoint spId = con.setSavepoint();<br>spId.getSavepointId();<br>Savepoint spName = con.setSavepoint("mySavepoint");<br>spName.getSavepointName();</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21027 (SQLSTATE: HV000): Cannot execute the query in auto-commit mode**

<a id="9604d9173d6629c6"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">This error occurs when using commit, rollback, savepoint in the connection object created in the auto commit mode.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Change the connection object to auto commit false, or do not use commit, rollback, saveponit.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21028 (SQLSTATE: 24000): Invalid cursor position**

<a id="29b93550abc12d7d"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The cursor location is not valid when retrieving the data from ResultSet object.<br>The following is the code retrieving the data from the cursor location in which ResultSet object was created and invalid. An error occurs while retrieving the data.<br>ResultSet rs = stmt.executeQuery("SELECT * FROM TEST");<br>int c1 = rs.getInt(1);</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Retrieve the data after relocating the cursor of ResultSet object.<br>The following is the code retrieving the data after relocating the cursor of ResultSet object from the code above.<br>ResultSet rs = stmt.executeQuery( "SELECT * FROM TEST" );<br>if( rs.next() )<br>{<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;int c1 = rs.getInt(1);<br>}</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21029 (SQLSTATE: HV000): No column has been read**

<a id="ed1692cf606044e3"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It tried to check null without retrieving the data from ResultSet object.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>wasNull method in ResultSet class can be called after retrieving the data.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21030 (SQLSTATE: HV000): Encoding error: [%s]**

<a id="9b19d09ff6a4fd18"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The error occurred while encoding the string with the character set used by the connection object.<br>The following is the code executed by entering UTF-16 data into PreparedStatement object which uses UTF8 character set. The error occurs while encoding in execute method.<br>char[] chars = {(char)0xD800};<br>Reader reader = new CharArrayReader(chars);<br>pstmt.setCharacterStream(&nbsp;&nbsp;1, reader );<br>pstmt.execute();</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check if the string type data character set and the character set used by the connection object are convertible each other.<br>GoldilocksConnection class can get the information about the character set by providing getCharset, getCharsetId, getCharsetName methods.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21031 (SQLSTATE: HV000): Decoding error: [%s]**

<a id="f0baf84299b79f12"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The error occurred while decoding the string with the character set used by the connection object.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check if the string type data character set and the character set used by the connection object are convertible each other.<br>GoldilocksConnection class can get the information about the character set by providing getCharset, getCharsetId, getCharsetName methods.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21032 (SQLSTATE: HV000): Stream error: [%s]**

<a id="dab7c5ac6d3643c3"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The stream object used as the data argument is not valid.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the open status of the stream object or if there is the data to read.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21033 (SQLSTATE: HV000): Trying to read the deleted row**

<a id="e39f2de785fb5db5"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>ResultSet object created as TYPE_SCROLL_SENSITIVE type read the data, but the data was deleted.<br>The following is the code reading ResultSet object, deleting the data, and reading ResultSet object again. An error occurs when it tries to read it again after deleting it because it is ResultSet object created as TYPE_SCROLL_SENSITIVE type.<br>Statement deleteStmt = con.createStatement();<br>Statement fetchStmt = con.createStatement( ResultSet.TYPE_SCROLL_SENSITIVE, ResultSet.CONCUR_READ_ONLY );<br>ResultSet rs = fetchStmt.executeQuery( "SELECT * FROM TEST" );<br>while( rs.next() ) {<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;System.out.println( "ID = " + rs.getString( 1 ) );<br>}<br>deleteStmt.executeQuery( "DELETE FROM TEST WHERE ID = 100" );<br>rs.absolute(0);<br>while( rs.next() ) {<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;rs.getString( 1 );<br>}</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>This error may occur when using SCROLL_SENSITIVE type ResultSet.<br>The fetch size of SCROLL_SENSITVE type ResultSet is fixed to 100.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21034 (SQLSTATE: HV000): Invalid interval format string: [%s]**

<a id="4e33476ab2b906f7"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21035 (SQLSTATE: HV000): The Statement has an opened ResultSet**

<a id="e2d5116ba6f87bb0"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">It tried to set the cursor name through the statement object, but there was already an open ResultSet.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Set the cursor name before opening ResultSet.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21036 (SQLSTATE: HV000): The RowId object is unknown**

<a id="47cec1e79f4b2ba6"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The data used as a parameter argument is not RowId object.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Use the valid RowId object.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21037 (SQLSTATE: 08000): The failover failed**

<a id="3688cf708a58cbc4"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The connection property alternate_servers was set and the communication protocol was disconnected, so it tried failover, but the failover failed.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check the connection information used in the connection property alternate_servers.<br>Check the network environment of the alternative server.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21038 (SQLSTATE: 07009): The parameterIndex is not valid: [%s]**

<a id="20f22a24c1fc18ac"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The parameter number is not valid.<br>The following is an example of using CallableStatement class. The number 1 parameter is an output type and the number 2 parameter is an input type in SQL statement.<br><br>CallableStatement cstmt = con.prepareCall( "SELECT NAME INTO ? FROM SAMPLE WHERE ID = ?");<br>cstmt.registerOutParameter(1, Types.VARCHAR);<br>cstmt.setInt(2, 100);<br>cstmt.execute();<br>System.out.println( cstmt.getString(1) );<br><br>If the number other than 1 ,2 is used in the example above for the parameter number in the data set function, then this error occurs.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the number of parameters and the parameter number in SQL statement.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21039 (SQLSTATE: HY000): No data read**

<a id="35abb282ebcb0b59"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>wasNull method was called without reading the data from CallableStatement object.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Read the data first before calling wasNull method.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21040 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Invalid locator protocol version**

<a id="9453eb1d4a342308"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>It tried to communicate with glocator to configure the global connection but the communication protocol version does not match.<br>The global connection configuration using glocator uses the connection property locator_host, locator_port.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Use the same version glocator.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21041 (SQLSTATE: HY000): not matched locator protocol command sequence number**

<a id="daea9d3f735b34d4"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>glocator protocol was sent to configure the global connection, but the protocol number does not match.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Set the connection property alternate_locator in preparation for the packet loss or the communication failure.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21042 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Unable to open the file '%s'**

<a id="e3f94d18f80ac40e"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The file does not exist.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the file path and name.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21043 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Unable to read the file '%s'**

<a id="03ef4698833c3050"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>IO exception occurred while reading the file.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the privilege, loss or existence of the file.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21044 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Unable to close the file '%s'**

<a id="49ba3bcc518059b6"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>IO exception occurred while closing the file.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the privilege, loss or existence of the file.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21045 (SQLSTATE: HY000): invalid INI file format**

<a id="218529acf07be977"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The locator file format is not a correct INI file format.<br>The following is an example of the locator file in the correct INI format.<br><br>[G1N1]<br>HOST = 127.0.0.1<br>PORT = 22581<br>DB_HOME = g1n1_home<br>[G2N1]<br>HOST = 127.0.0.1<br>PORT = 22582<br>DB_HOME = g2n2_home</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Modify the file to a correct INI format.<br>The member name should be enclosed in [ and ]. List the member property under the name.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21046 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Parameter[%s]'s input data type is mismatched with output data type**

<a id="b5415af4be7b8a69"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The output parameter type and the data type are not compatible when using CallableStatement object.<br>The following code sets the data in int type in CallableStatement object and set the out parameter as VARCHAR type. An error occurs because types are not compatible.<br>CallableStatement cstmt = con.prepareCall( "CALL SAMPLE_PROC( ? )" );<br>cstmt.setInt( 1, 100 );<br>cstmt.registerOutParameter( 1, Types.VARCHAR );<br>cstmt.execute();</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>If input and output parameter types are used simultaneously as the code above, then the types should be compatible.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21047 (SQLSTATE: 40001): Retry the transactional operations again**

<a id="26b2675c88cb7641"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The transaction occurred in the global connection environment, but it was disconnected.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Execute the operation again.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21048 (SQLSTATE: 08006): Unable to get cluster system information**

<a id="f8d084061748872f"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>It tried to configure the connection in the global connection environment, but there was a member which could not JOIN.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the member which could not JOIN, and respond to it.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21049 (SQLSTATE: HY000): The Statement does not have a ResultSet**

<a id="fe319593edd3a027"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>If ResultSet does not exist when executeQuery method of PreparedStatement or CallableStatement class is called, then an error occurs.<br>The following code executes SELECT statement but the statement does not have ResultSet, so an error occurs when calling executeQuery method.<br>CallableStatement cstmt = con.prepareCall( "SELECT NAME INTO ? FROM WHERE ID = ? " );<br><br>con.registerOutParameter( 1, Types.VARCHAR );<br>con.setInt( 2, 100 );<br>con.executeQuery();</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Use execute or executeUpdate method for SQL without ResultSet.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21050 (SQLSTATE: 08006): Unable to get location information**

<a id="6505aa2ea4ad1eee"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The connection property locator_file is missing, or locator_host or locator_port is missing when using the global connection.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Set locator_file, locator_host or locator_port when using the global connection.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21051 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Not exist node information - %s**

<a id="6ab19cce74948c8f"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The member information does not exist in the location file or glocator.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Add the connection information of the member to the location file or glocator.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21052 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Operation on freed LOB**

<a id="6f2c264ae1c37ebc"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>LOB object was freed before executing the operation.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If LOB object is freed, then the executable operation is limited.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21053 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Invalid sql : %s**

<a id="59699fedb30646d8"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>It tried to create PreparedStaetment with RETURN_GENERATED_KEYS option, but the statement is not INSERT statement.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>RETURN_GENERATED_KEYS option can be used only in INSERT statement.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21054 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Can not combine auto-generated keys with batch update**

<a id="00c562c1d9a5a61d"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The batch-related function was used in the statement which used the auto generated key.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">The auto generated key and the batch-related function can not be used together.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21055 (SQLSTATE: HY000): An error occurred while using the SSL function : %s**

<a id="6646fe113c7d1abb"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>An error occurred in API while using SSL security protocol.<br><br>The error may occur because of the version mismatch, certificate error, encoding algorithm support problem, key management error, network error, or Java version.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check the error message, and respond to it.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **21056 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Invalid column type**

<a id="2b1f524de3087e58"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The object type of the data which was input while setting the data type to Types.NULL when setting parameters is not supported by Goldilocks JDBC.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Check the type which is supported by Goldilocks JDBC.<br>Refer to<a href="../part-05-developer-manual/35-jdbc.md#1f1a9557cf30f535">Type Conversion</a>.</td></tr></tbody></table>

<a id="f81c1a31d9e5f621"></a>
## Embedded SQL Related Error

<a id="1147ecf74e74233a"></a>
### Embedded SQL Run-time Library Related Error

> **23000 (SQLSTATE: 42000): syntax error**

<a id="17888da443caece7"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23001 (SQLSTATE: 0A000): feature not supported**

<a id="506a26896d9d4a10"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23002 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Bind variable "%s" was not declared**

<a id="b82a8d82044cb602"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23003 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Application can't be initialized**

<a id="07e3704866c7626c"></a>
