<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">An error occurred during initializing the embedded SQL library.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">An error occurred due to the failure during the memory allocation or semaphore creation. Check the related system environment according to the error message.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23004 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Application can't be finalized**

<a id="64319bd25948a05f"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">An error occurred during finalizing the embedded SQL library.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">An error occurred due to the failure during deallocating the allocated memory or freeing the created semaphore. Check the related system environment according to the error message.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23005 (SQLSTATE: RD000): Service is not available**

<a id="00198e58f4aa2987"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23006 (SQLSTATE: RD000): Statement is not prepared**

<a id="ffd1ce36880e64b8"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23007 (SQLSTATE: 08001): Client can't establish SQL-connection**

<a id="e66158733ea39d07"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">After an embedded SQL library failed to initialize the operation, the application continued without error handling.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">If it failed to initialize the operation, restart the application.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23008 (SQLSTATE: HY000): cursor "%s" is not open**

<a id="6b64fa17bbfeb097"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It tried to FETCH or CLOSE a cursor even when the cursor is not open.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Open the cursor first.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23009 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Application can't create semaphore**

<a id="aceaade2ef846f94"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It failed to create the semaphore during initializing the embedded SQL library.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the system error number and the system environment.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23010 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Application can't destroy semaphore**

<a id="8ad9cdf8eb7d61b4"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It failed to destroy the semaphore during terminating the embedded SQL library.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the system error number and respond to it.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23011 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Application can't create allocator**

<a id="5414b2109f38d735"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It failed to create the memory manager during initializing the embedded SQL library.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the system error number and the system environment.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23012 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Application can't destroy allocator**

<a id="3bed31999a7e614c"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It failed to delete the memory manager during terminating the embedded SQL library.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the system error number and respond to it.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23013 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Application can't create symbol table**

<a id="01e13dacfc80b1eb"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It failed to create the symbol table due to the insufficient memory.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the system memory.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23014 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Application can't destroy symbol table**

<a id="6b9478a4284231b0"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It failed to destroy the symbol table.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the system error number and respond to it.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23015 (SQLSTATE: IM004): Driver's SQLAllocHandle on SQL_HANDLE_ENV failed**

<a id="2efdd9c79374529b"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It failed to create the SQL_HANDLE_ENV handle of ODBC.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check system memory size and odbc.ini file.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23016 (SQLSTATE: IM001): Driver does not support ODBC 3.0**

<a id="08ed2a21d4f73e60"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The ODBC driver does not support version 3.0.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the ODBC driver.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23017 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Application can't allocate memory**

<a id="2c9b513b433a65aa"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It failed to allocate the memory.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the system memory.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23018 (SQLSTATE: 42000): Statement "%s" was not prepared**

<a id="52a676b35092c5b4"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">It tried to EXECUTE, OPEN, FETCH or CLOSE the statement with the given name when it was not prepared.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Execute PREPARE statement first.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23019 (SQLSTATE: 42000): Descriptor name is too long**

<a id="9e923b11796d76b1"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The length of the descriptor name exceeds 128.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Use the name whose length is 128 or below.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23020 (SQLSTATE: HYC00): Not implemented feature, in a function %s**

<a id="5ec333a0ca473c64"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It tried to execute the feature which is not supported.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Find the workaround for a feature which is not supported.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23021 (SQLSTATE: 07004): USING clause required for dynamic parameters**

<a id="c5032c73052b8488"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">USING clause was not used in the EXECUTE or OPEN statement which is a dynamic method statement using the prepared statement with the parameter.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Use a USING clause in EXECUTE or OPEN statement.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23022 (SQLSTATE: 07001): USING clause: illegal variable name/number**

<a id="b25aac3d77782b93"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The number of host variables in USING clause is bigger than the number of parameters in the prepared statement.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">The number of parameters should be the same as the number of the host variables.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23023 (SQLSTATE: 07001): USING clause: not all variables bound**

<a id="49100f776869afc7"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The number of host variables in USING clause is smaller than the number of parameters in the prepared statement.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">The number of parameters should be the same as the number of the host variables.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23024 (SQLSTATE: 07007): INTO clause required for result fields**

<a id="4f972edc20f6c4dd"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">INTO clause was not used in the EXECUTE statement which is a dynamic method statement using the prepared statement with the column.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Use a INTO clause in EXECUTE statement.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23025 (SQLSTATE: 07001): INTO clause: illegal variable name/number**

<a id="b1a0692fa2c8be07"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The number of host variables in INTO clause is bigger than the number of columns in the prepared statement.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">The number of columns should be the same as the number of the host variables.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23026 (SQLSTATE: 07001): INTO clause: not all variables bound**

<a id="f3b0019a9b31924e"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The number of host variables in INTO clause is smaller than the number of columns in the prepared statement.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">The number of columns should be the same as the number of the host variables.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23027 (SQLSTATE: 22002): null value, no indicator parameter**

<a id="8f50df367b711253"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">It tried to return NULL data without using a host variable for INDICATOR.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Use the host variable for INDICATOR. Alternatively, use gspec option unsafe-null during the build process.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23028 (SQLSTATE: 07005): cursor "%s" statement is not a query**

<a id="b1abfb4838966141"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The prepared statement which executed OPEN statement in the dynamic method is not a query.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Check the syntax of the prepared statement which tried to execute OPEN statement, and modify it accordingly.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23029 (SQLSTATE: 08003): connection not open**

<a id="e9eb9a00d9265c49"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It executed the embedded SQL while DB is disconnected.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the connection status of DB.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23030 (SQLSTATE: 34000): cursor "%s" is not updatable**

<a id="c32452b22e1428ca"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The cursor used in UPDATE or DELETE statement is not updatable.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Use FOR UPDATE clause when declaring a cursor.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23031 (SQLSTATE: 08002): connection name "%s" in use**

<a id="26c31fb244e445ae"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The connection with the given name already exists.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Try it after changing the name.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23032 (SQLSTATE: 08002): duplicate connection context**

<a id="5a1e580cffa2db20"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It tried to connect to the context, and the context was already connected.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Handle it accordingly.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23033 (SQLSTATE: HY000): GROUPID type is only available with global connection**

<a id="9ea9c65332d19417"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23034 (SQLSTATE: 42000): SELECT INTO or RETURN INTO returns too many rows**

<a id="00192bae57ee7b4f"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">It executed RETURN INTO statement as an array in SELECT INTO or DML, but the number of rows is bigger than the array size.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Make the array size bigger.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23035 (SQLSTATE: 24000): cursor "%s" is not declared**

<a id="c115539a67747ee4"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It used undeclared cursor in OPEN statement.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Declare the cursor with DECLARE statement before executing OPEN statement.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23036 (SQLSTATE: 24000): cursor "%s" is not closed**

<a id="28694737f1e360bb"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It used the opened cursor in DECLARE statement.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the cursor status and handle it accordingly.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23037 (SQLSTATE: 24000): cursor "%s" is already opened**

<a id="a2b23cd8d01ace29"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It tried to open the opened cursor again in a standing cursor.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the cursor status and handle it accordingly.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23038 (SQLSTATE: 24000): cursor "%s" is not a dynamic cursor**

<a id="e845abcd4be00c90"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The host variable was used even though the cursor used in OPEN statement was declared without using a dynamic SQL.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Declare the cursor by using a dynamic SQL again, or do not use the host variable.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23039 (SQLSTATE: HY000): invalid cursor**

<a id="99618e81dfa02124"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>SQL_CURSOR type host variable has NULL value.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Allocate SQL_CURSOR and get a cursor.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23040 (SQLSTATE: 07000): Attempt to allocate existing descriptor**

<a id="26f25656eb904195"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It attempts to allocate the existing descriptor again.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Free the descriptor to allocate the existing descriptor again.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23041 (SQLSTATE: 07000): "%s" invalid descriptor**

<a id="48591dea214984fc"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The descriptor with the given name does not exist.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Set the correct descriptor name.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23042 (07009): invalid descriptor index**

<a id="06a47c1ebd9a5d98"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">In the GET or SET statement, the column index value exceeds the occurrence range or is below 0.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Set the correct column index value, or allocate the descriptor with a bigger occurrence again.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23043 (SQLSTATE: 07000): Insufficient item descriptor areas**

<a id="2af43f0b4b1f00ab"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The number of parameters or columns in SQL is bigger than the occurrence value of the descriptor.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Allocate the bigger occurrence value of the descriptor.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23044 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Descriptor is not proper parameter list**

<a id="600f2d15be8deefe"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The number of the descriptor's parameters is smaller than the expected parameter value in SQL.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Set the descriptor by executing DESCRIBE statement, or manually set the descriptor.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23045 (SQLSTATE: 07000): Descriptor is not proper select list**

<a id="59aff563b3a87913"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The number of the descriptor's columns is smaller than the expected column value in SQL.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Set the descriptor by executing DESCRIBE statement, or manually set the descriptor.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23046 (SQLSTATE: 07006): invalid data type for descriptor**

<a id="fe5717cd24e5438a"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>TYPE in SET statement is wrong.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Use the correct SQL TYPE.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23047 (SQLSTATE: 07006): The host variable type are not compatible with descriptor's type**

<a id="8e1464525ad9cd73"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The host variable type which was used to get DATA in GET statement is not compatible.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Use the host variable which is compatible with DATA.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23048 (SQLSTATE: 07000): Encountered zero length in ANSI dynamic SET statement**

<a id="abeb0305c68027ea"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>LENGTH value is below 0 in SET statement.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Set LENGTH value to a value bigger than 0.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23049 (SQLSTATE: 07000): invalid SQLDA**

<a id="f5e0283a7061fea0"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">SQLDA used in the statement is NULL, so it is not valid.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Allocate SQLDA by using SQLSQLDAAlloc function before executing the statement.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **23050 (SQLSTATE: 22000): invalid length with variable character or binary**

<a id="e06158ed82a44baf"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">This error occurs when a negative value is set for the len member variable of the structure that contains a VARCHAR or VARBINARY variable used within a .gc file. This error is only detected when the variable is used as an IN or IN_OUT parameter of a procedure.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Execute the program after setting the len member of the VARCHAR or VARBINARY variable to the actual (non-negative) data length.</td></tr></tbody></table>

<a id="2de9204e1e5d45a6"></a>
### Embedded SQL Pre-compile Related Error

> **41000 (SQLSTATE: 42000): syntax error**

<a id="3a7a7f1ccd0c2eb1"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The syntax in the error message is wrong.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Modify the syntax in the error message.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41001 (SQLSTATE: 0A000): feature not supported**

<a id="e0adb9da0bafe2e6"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The syntax used is not support.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">The syntax in which an error occurred is not support, so use the alternative syntax which is supported.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41002 (SQLSTATE: 42000): Host variable "%s" not declared**

<a id="021c78cd443aaea7"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The host variable is not declared.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Declare the host variable in DECLARE SECTION.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41003 (SQLSTATE: 42000): Cursor "%s" not declared**

<a id="fad39ae844b21947"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41004 (SQLSTATE: 42000): "%s": file not exist**

<a id="7864e65b23d49e97"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The header file used in INCLUDE statement does not exist.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the header file name and modify it.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41005 (SQLSTATE: 42000): expression type does not match usage**

<a id="66c6d04542ef997e"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The host variable used in the statement in which an error occurred is not compatible with the variable type used in the statement.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Modify the host variable type.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41006 (SQLSTATE: 42000): Fatal error while doing embedded SQL preprocessing**

<a id="9f66fce6932bd258"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>An error occurred while parsing the SQL statement.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Correctly modify the SQL statement.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41007 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Precompiler can't create symbol table**

<a id="a123f0caab35915a"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It failed to create the symbol table.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the system error number and deal with it.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41008 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Precompiler can't destroy symbol table**

<a id="28730638dc139abc"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It failed to destroy the symbol table.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the system error number and deal with it.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41009 (SQLSTATE: 42000): identifier is too long**

<a id="f601776077794248"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The length of the identifier name exceeds 128.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>The length of the identifier name should be smaller than 128.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41010 (SQLSTATE: 42000): token "%s" is not valid in preprocessor expressions**

<a id="0c536a006f19063d"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The string using double quote (") was used as an argument in the function macro of the preprocessor.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">The argument in the function macro does not support the string using the double quote (").</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41011 (SQLSTATE: 42000): multi-character character constant**

<a id="a2e095d4e29ae6a7"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">Two or more characters were used to express the character constant using double quote (") in the preprocessor.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">The length of the character constant using double quote (") should be 1.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41012 (SQLSTATE: 42000): floating constant in preprocessor expression**

<a id="be76f658a24f6015"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The real number was declared as a constant in preprocessor.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>The preprocessor does not support the real number constant.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41013 (SQLSTATE: 42000): invalid suffix "%s" on integer constant**

<a id="e40ac9c719c58b44"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>An invalid suffix was used for the integer constant in the preprocessor.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Only u, U, l, L are the allowed suffixes for the integer constant.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41014 (SQLSTATE: 42000): cursor name "%s" already declared**

<a id="59ac990463cae48b"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41015 (SQLSTATE: 07004): cursor "%s" is not a dynamic cursor**

<a id="7c96788e303ab729"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The cursor has already been declared as a static cursor.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Deprecated</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41016 (SQLSTATE: 42000): "%s" has no member named "%s"**

<a id="46599f9a929f70b0"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The host variable is not the member variable of the structure.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the variable name and modify it correctly.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41017 (SQLSTATE: 42000): storage size of "%s" isn't known**

<a id="3506ddc68b2f855f"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41018 (SQLSTATE: 42000): variable "%s" must be integer type**

<a id="0ee89f2db282e1b7"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The host variable used in the statement is not an integer type.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Change the host variable type to the integer type.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41019 (SQLSTATE: 42000): variable "%s" must be string type**

<a id="bece57b1d71eea1e"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The host variable used in the statement is not a string type.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Change the host variable type to the string type.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41020 (SQLSTATE: 42000): invalid indicator variable type: indicator variable "%s" must have numeric type(char/short/int/long)**

<a id="81ee863f9e5b4840"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The host variable type used as an indicator is incorrect.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Only char, short, int, long types are allowed for the host variable used as an indicator.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41021 (SQLSTATE: 42000): duplicate "%s"**

<a id="6c8bdb463371d21a"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The keyword the same as the type qualifier is duplicate in the host variable declaration.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check whether the duplicate keywords exist and modify it.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41022 (SQLSTATE: 42000): both "%s" and "%s" in declaration specifiers**

<a id="47e2d347be4adae4"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">Long was declared more than twice in the long long declaration of the host variable declaration.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Check whether long is declared more than twice in the host variable declaration, and modify it.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41023 (SQLSTATE: 42000): two or more data types in declaration specifiers**

<a id="259f943797ae82fd"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>Data types were mixed and used together in the host variable declaration.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Deprecated</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41024 (SQLSTATE: 42000): C++ punctuation sequences are not permitted**

<a id="7e0fdab62b7b20f1"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>Host variable was declared with c++ syntax.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Colon (:) can not be used for the host variable declaration.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41025 (SQLSTATE: 42000): host variable expression has invalid type**

<a id="f892970348942ab1"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The type of the host variable used in the statement is invalid.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the type of the host variable and modify it.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41026 (SQLSTATE: 42000): typedef "%s" has invalid**

<a id="243a251aebcd4124"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The type declared with typedef is invalid.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Only secondary array is allowed for char type and primary array is allowed for other types when declaring a type with typedef.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41027 (SQLSTATE: 42000): too many 'define' macro (%d)**

<a id="6875bd1758b73b38"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41028 (SQLSTATE: 42000): '%s' macro is already defined at line %d, in file %s**

<a id="09416f7f57c58535"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The macro has already been defined.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the macro in which the error occurred and modify it.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41029 (SQLSTATE: 42000): missing host variable**

<a id="8747b9b8139347f1"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">Only a colon (:) was written and the host variable was missing in the statement in which the error occurred.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Check the error statement and modify it.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41030 (SQLSTATE: 42000): invalid getting groupid variable type: variable "%s" must have signed numeric type**

<a id="8e7ddf42595871ed"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The host variable used in GET CLUSTER_GROUP_ID statement is not a signed integer type.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Use a signed integer type host variable in GET CLUSTER_GROUP_ID statement.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41031 (SQLSTATE: 42000): invalid sql statement: getting groupid is available with select/update/delete/insert statement**

<a id="23508cf3172477bc"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">SQL other than SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE, INSERT was used in GET CLUSTER_GROUP_ID statement.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Use only SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE, INSERT in GET CLUSTER_GROUP_ID statement.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41032 (SQLSTATE: HY000): cursor variable type can not use an array**

<a id="e03f64a9d09447f2"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>SQL_CURSOR type host variable is declared in an array.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Do not declare SQL_CURSOR type host variable in an array.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41033 (SQLSTATE: 42000): Invalid type for %s descriptor item host variable**

<a id="29af7269d00a9a22"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The host variable type which is not suitable for an item was used in an ansi descriptor.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Use the host variable type which is suitable for an item.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41034 (SQLSTATE: 42000): Invalid combination of descriptor and non-descriptor clauses**

<a id="ef73b593788ff4a2"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The descriptor clause and the non-descriptor clause are used together in a dynamic SQL statement.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Do not use the descriptor clause and the non-descriptor clause together in a dynamic SQL statement.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41035 (SQLSTATE: 42000): variable "%s" for the descriptor's indicator must have the same size as SQLLEN**

<a id="ce24552d13282de3"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The indicator host variable size which is to be used in a descriptor is different from SQLLEN size.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Declare the type of the host variable used as an indicator the same as SQLLEN size.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41036 (SQLSTATE: 42000): Expecting a value between 1 and 65535 inclusive**

<a id="be097395f39f3000"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>When allocating the ansi descriptor, the occurrence range is incorrect.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Set the occurrence range from 1 to 65535. (Default value: 100)</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41037 (SQLSTATE: 42000): invalid descriptor index**

<a id="4d097cd714552cd8"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The column index value below 0 was used in an ansi descriptor-related statement.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Set the column index to the value bigger than 0.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **41038 (SQLSTATE: 42000): preprocessor with no expression**

<a id="56bc149f80f256ff"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The preprocessor macro is defined, but no value has been assigned to it. As shown in the example code, if a value is not assigned to the macro, the conditional statements may not be evaluated correctly.<br><br>#define ___AAA___<br>#if ___AAA___ == 0<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;VARCHAR var;<br>#else<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;char var;<br>#endif</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">When using a preprocessor macro, a value that can be clearly evaluated as true or false must be assigned. Modify the value to ensure correct evaluation in conditional statements.</td></tr></tbody></table>

<a id="d75af03fa0d9dbb7"></a>
## Communication Related Error

<a id="67a89e1e6dcb8729"></a>
### Communication Related error

> **24000 (SQLSTATE: 08S01): Communication link failure**

<a id="26546e9821abdb0d"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The network connection was lost.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the network status and reconnect.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **24001 (SQLSTATE: 08S01): Invalid communication protocol**

<a id="c2fe6a788b10a171"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">There was an error in the communication protocol format, or the data was corrupted or tampered with during network transmission.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Use a client library that is compatible with the server, or check the network connection status.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **24002 (SQLSTATE: 22000): Invalid GOLDILOCKS_DATA Directory**

<a id="2ac4de94adc1f886"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The directory specified by the environment variable GOLDILOCKS_DATA is incorrect.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Verify the value of the environment variable GOLDILOCKS_DATA.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **24003 (SQLSTATE: 22000): not supported function**

<a id="22d9573be54bc64e"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **24004 (SQLSTATE: 22000): Invalid interprocess protocol**

<a id="8ab7e9b42b3eb0bb"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The IPC communication version is not compatible.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Use a client version that is compatible with the server.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **24005 (SQLSTATE: 22000): Unable to attach the shared memory segment. unable to access the file '%s'**

<a id="41d1926d6da6eed2"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">This error occurs when the $GOLDILOCKS_HOME/conf/shmstatic_info file cannot be accessed.<br>This file is created when the server starts up, and all server processes use the information in this file to attach to the SSA.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Restarting the server will recreate the shmstatic_info file.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **24006 (SQLSTATE: HV090): Invalid string length or buffer length**

<a id="a9939e26b075bf3a"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">This error occurs when the buffer size is smaller than the length of the string to be received during communication between the client and server.<br>It can occur if, during internal protocol processing, the server or client misinterprets the message length or attempts to receive data larger than expected.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **24007 (SQLSTATE: 22000): not matched command sequence number**

<a id="5bc10d3bb506cb86"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">When using the User Datagram Protocol (UDP), packets may be lost depending on the network environment. This error occurs when a command request or response packet is lost, causing the command sequence numbers between the client and server to become inconsistent.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Since the missing command may not have been processed correctly, the same command should be resent for re-execution.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **24008 (SQLSTATE: HYT01): Connection timeout expired**

<a id="e05b51ff54429515"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>An error such as EAGAIN occurred during communication.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>This is an internally controlled error.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **24009 (SQLSTATE: 08001): SSL connection failed**

<a id="9a4b2ac01197e9e5"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">Failed to establish an SSL encrypted connection.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Check whether the OpenSSL versions of the client and server are compatible, and verify that a valid certificate is properly configured on the server.</td></tr></tbody></table>

<a id="b0ff8c5a7db4a610"></a>
### Server Communication Related Error

> **52000 (SQLSTATE: 08S01): Communication link failure**

<a id="2fb6bc08b286af1f"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The IPC channel was initialized before the database was fully started.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the status of the shared memory and restart the database.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **52001 (SQLSTATE: 08000): Invalid communication protocol**

<a id="c0b244ca08100a68"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The communication protocol version between the client and server is not compatible.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Use a client library that is compatible with the server version.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **52002 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Not enough cm unit memory**

<a id="8220d521224e2ce1"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">A communication buffer shortage has occurred due to the transmission of a large volume of data or the simultaneous execution of many queries.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Increase the value of MAXIMUM_SESSION_CM_BUFFER_SIZE in the configuration file, or optimize queries to prevent unnecessary transmission of large amounts of data.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **52003 (SQLSTATE: HY000): exceeded maximum packet allocation timeout**

<a id="e5f8d7dc3e47c534"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">Under high load, excessive concurrent connections or large data transfers may cause delays in packet allocation.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Increase the values of BLOCK_READ_COUNT or CLUSTER_PACKET_ALLOCATION_TIMEOUT in the configuration file.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **52004 (SQLSTATE: 08001): exceeded maximum number of ipc channels**

<a id="33ee210d2ff5d8dc"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The maximum number of available IPC channels has been exceeded.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Increase the value of IPC_CHNNEL_COUNT in the configuration file.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **52005 (SQLSTATE: HYT00): Timeout expired**

<a id="136583d1380dd0db"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The specified timeout period was exceeded during network communication.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Adjust the timeout settings on the server and client, or check the firewall and network equipment.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **52006 (SQLSTATE: 08001): Unable to open certificate or key file : %s**

<a id="bcba5a5aeff56177"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">Unable to open the SSL certificate file or private key file.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Check whether the SSL certificate and private key files exist, verify that the file paths are correct, and ensure the certificate file format is valid.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **52007 (SQLSTATE: 08001): SSL connection failed**

<a id="7d4ad3cb83dc2456"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">Failed to establish a secure SSL connection.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Verify that the OpenSSL library is properly installed on the server and that the SSL certificate and private key files are valid.</td></tr></tbody></table>

<a id="96970cc0b776d094"></a>

<a id="d070485daf416274"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>deprecated</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>If this error occurs, contact our customer service department.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **25003 (SQLSTATE: 08000): Invalid protocol**

<a id="7e21cdf8ad39fe86"></a>

> **25006 (SQLSTATE: HY000): remote session is not opened**

> **25007 (SQLSTATE: 42000): the property '%s' of cluster member '%s' is not compatible with the cluster system**

<a id="850cba9293ceb7d9"></a>

> **25008 (SQLSTATE: 42000): the scn '%s' of cluster member '%s' is mismatch**

<a id="89413b5d84ad66d5"></a>

> **25009 (SQLSTATE: HY000): number of shared servers must be greater than or equal to number of request queues**

<a id="de2301234b80131b"></a>

<a id="19e5e548fe8c66fe"></a>

<a id="22f300283f5ef68d"></a>
## Foreign Function Related Error

> **26000 (SQLSTATE: 07006) the external type is not appropriate for the parameter**

<a id="a3146add7f6763da"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">An attempt was made to convert the datatype of the routine parameter to the datatype of the specified external parameter, but it failed.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Specify the convertible external datatype or parameter datatype.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **26001 (SQLSTATE: 07006) Incorrect Usage of MAXLEN in parameters clause**

<a id="f8b800cf6791d81e"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">MAXLEN keyword was incorrectly used in PARAMETER clause.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">MAXLEN can be declared only for routine parameters of CHAR or BINARY family datatypes of OUT, IN OUT, or RETURN type.<br>Only numeric type is allowed for the external datatype of MAXLEN.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **26002 (SQLSTATE: 07006) Incorrect Usage of LENGTH in parameters clause**

<a id="b204e343192b2c64"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>LENGTH keyword was incorrectly used in PARAMETER clause.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">LENGTH can be declared only for formal parameters of CHAR or BINARY family datatypes.<br>Only numeric type is allowed for the external datatype of MAXLEN.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **26003 (SQLSTATE: 07006) Invalid external type specification for INDICATOR**

<a id="915815af1b6874f3"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The external datatype for INDICATOR is wrong.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Only numeric type is allowed for the external datatype of INDICATOR.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **26004 (SQLSTATE: 22003) numeric overflow**

<a id="8f820038be59355c"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>If evaluating the value expression, then overflow/underflow occurs.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Alter the external parameter datatype or the routine parameter datatype.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **26005 (SQLSTATE: 22027) Length Mismatch for CHAR or BINARY data**

<a id="b7a00f9b827a1520"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td>The routine parameter length is smaller than the external parameter length.<br>The parameter length is smaller than the external parameter length.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td>Alter the routine parameter length.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **26006 (SQLSTATE: 39000) failed to open library(%s)**

<a id="6819a82538cb8d9e"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>It failed to open the dynamic link library.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the path of the dynamic link library.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **26007 (SQLSTATE: 39000) invalid datetime format**

<a id="8760d2c9e26026e3"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>The date/time format of the external parameter is wrong.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the date/time value of the external parameter.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **26008 (SQLSTATE: HY000) failed to start up a process 'gextproc'**

<a id="ef01b0a47457ca0f"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">It failed to start 'gextproc' process.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Check if the unix domain socket used in 'gextproc' is properly created in /tmp.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **26009 (SQLSTATE: 39000) lost connection to 'gextproc'**

<a id="7e20ecfee094206d"></a>

<a id="7f446844419eec47"></a>
## gsql/ gsqlnet Related Error

> **40000 (SQLSTATE: 42000): syntax error**

<a id="75a1de2f91b25c4b"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The SQL syntax is incorrect.<br><br>gSQL&gt; SELECT FROM t1;<br>ERR-42000(40000): syntax error:<br>SELECT FROM t1<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;^&nbsp;&nbsp;^<br>Error at line 1</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Comply with the SQL syntax.<br><br>gSQL&gt; SELECT c1 FROM t1;<br>C1<br>--<br>&nbsp;1<br>1 row selected.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **40001 (SQLSTATE: 0A000): feature not supported**

<a id="fdc65d07f298d5fa"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>This error code is used for internal tests.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>N/A</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **40002 (SQLSTATE: HY000): Bind variable "%s" not declared**

<a id="03f6390bae392e06"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">Bind variable is not declared.<br><br>gSQL&gt; SELECT c1 FROM t1 WHERE c1 = :v1;<br>ERR-HY000(40002): Bind variable "v1" not declared</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Declare and use the bind variable as shown below.<br><br>gSQL&gt; \var v1 INTEGER<br>gSQL&gt; \exec :v1 := 1<br>gSQL&gt; SELECT c1 FROM t1 WHERE c1 = :v1;<br>C1<br>--<br>&nbsp;1<br>1 row selected.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **40003 (SQLSTATE: 42000): "%s": table or view does not exist.**

<a id="fecb67b42c886f78"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">This error occurs if the table is dropped while executing the following gSQL command.<br><br>gSQL&gt; \desc t1</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">If the command is executed again after the DROP is completed, the following error occurs.<br><br>gSQL&gt; \desc t1<br>ERR-42000(16040): table or view does not exist :<br>SELECT *&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;FROM T1@LOCAL&nbsp;&nbsp;WHERE 1 = 0<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;*<br>ERROR at line 1:</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **40004 (SQLSTATE: 42000): "%s": index does not exist.**

<a id="8aa1f004afd03cb1"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">This error occurs when the specified index does not exist.<br><br>gSQL&gt; \idesc invalid_index<br>ERR-42000(40004): "INVALID_INDEX": index does not exist.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Use the correct index name.<br><br>gSQL&gt;&nbsp;&nbsp;\idesc idx1<br>COLUMN_NAME ORDINAL_POSITION IS_ASCENDING_ORDER IS_NULLS_FIRST<br>----------- ---------------- ------------------ --------------<br>C1&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;1 TRUE&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;FALSE</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **40005 (SQLSTATE: RD000): Service is not available**

<a id="d62b44a7b1debe37"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td>Cause</td><td>Failed to load the ODBC driver, so gsql cannot be used.</td></tr><tr><td>Action</td><td>Check the system resources.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **40006 (SQLSTATE: RD000): Statement is not prepared**

<a id="0a171b32a4c58dbe"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">The SQL statement was not prepared.<br><br>gSQL&gt; \exec<br>ERR-RD000(40006): Statement is not prepared.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Prepare the SQL statement first, then execute it using \exec as shown below.<br><br>gSQL&gt; \prepare sql SELECT c1 FROM t1 WHERE c1 = 1;<br>SQL prepared.<br><br>gSQL&gt; \exec<br>C1<br>--<br>&nbsp;1<br>1 row selected.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **40007 (SQLSTATE: 42000): '%s': duplicate statement**

<a id="bc56692637910bb2"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">This error occurs when defining the redundant statement name using the \alloc command in gSQL features.<br><br>gSQL&gt; \alloc stmt2<br><br>gSQL&gt; \alloc stmt2<br>ERR-42000(40007): 'stmt2': duplicate statement</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Use different names when using the \alloc command.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **40008 (SQLSTATE: 42000): '%s': statement does not exist**

<a id="445b3b8d4b65dd0e"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">This error occurs when using a non-existent statement name in a gSQL command.<br><br>gSQL&gt; \alloc stmt2<br>gSQL&gt; \free invalid<br><br>ERR-42000(40008): 'invalid': statement does not exist</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Use an existing statement name as follows.<br><br>gSQL&gt; \free stmt2<br>gSQL&gt;</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **40009 (SQLSTATE: 42000): '%s': statement is not prepared**

<a id="4bbfa329193e8773"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">This error occurs when executing an unprepared statement using the \use command in gSQL.<br><br>gSQL&gt; \alloc stmt1<br>gSQL&gt; \use stmt1 exec<br><br>ERR-42000(40009): 'stmt1': statement is not prepared</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Use after<em>prepare sql</em>&nbsp;as follows.<br><br>gSQL&gt; \use stmt1 prepare sql SELECT * FROM t1;<br>SQL prepared.<br><br>gSQL&gt; \use stmt1 exec<br>no rows selected.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **40010 (SQLSTATE: 42000): insufficient privileges**

<a id="80111ea365bcd036"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">This error occurs when executing a gSQL command that requires specific privileges, as follows.<br><br>gSQL&gt; \connect u1 u1<br>gSQL&gt; \shutdown<br>ERR-42000(40010): insufficient privileges</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Connect as a user with the appropriate privileges to execute.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> **40011 (SQLSTATE: 42000): driver does not support %s function**

<a id="6a9f13d52ebfafa3"></a>
<table><tbody><tr><td valign="middle">Cause</td><td valign="middle">This error occurs when the ODBC function used in gSQL is not provided by the ODBC driver.</td></tr><tr><td valign="middle">Action</td><td valign="middle">Use an ODBC driver that supports the function.</td></tr></tbody></table>
